why: Both put the same five call sites through the one shared AsyncOpenAI client, but A's claims about Router mechanics are measured and controlled — caching is already delivered by the migration (so A deleted its own policy branch rather than ship a no-op), temperature is silently dropped on 36 catalog ids, fallbacks don't cover the 429/5xx/stream failures an agent loop actually hits — while B's two built improvements rest on exactly those unverified premises and its top-ranked 'quick-win' is probably a placebo. B is the better migration (it unlocks the operator's configured host, so the repo's own Anthropic-compatible default actually routes, with tests) and finds sharper app-internal problems, but 'loses: nothing' on a change that moves billing to the Router key and drops temperature is the kind of claim that costs a CTO trust in everything else in the report.
A_best: Replacing the 2024 MULTIMODAL_MODELS list with Router's catalog: a real correctness loss the migration exposes — on any current model ask_with_images() hard-errored and ask()/ask_tool() silently stripped the browser agent's screenshots — fixed, live-verified end to end, and failing closed for non-catalog models.
B_best: The retry-predicate fix: retry_if_exception_type((OpenAIError, Exception, ValueError)) matches everything, so the comment saying 'Don't retry TokenLimitExceeded' was false and an unclearable local error burned ~3 minutes of backoff; small diff, agent path updated, two new tests. Its i7 (the max_input_tokens guard enforced on cl100k guesses for a Claude deployment) and n1 (the shipped example model isn't a catalog id, so operators see no traffic and no error) are findings A missed.
A_worst: Internal inconsistency on what actually moves: the calls table lists all five sites as 'now: router' with the example default claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219, while i1 states Router serves none of the claude-3 ids — so with the shipped config and only api.openai.com unlocked by default, the real routed traffic is less than the summary implies, and A never raises that consequence. The live log also shows ask_with_images 0 ok / 6 error against the 'both 200' claim.
B_worst: Ranking prompt_cache_key as 'the biggest lever in the app and the cheapest to pull' with no without-policy arm — A's controlled arms show the runtime already sets a label-derived key and the policy adds nothing — and building a hard-coded cross-vendor fallback list for an unknown operator model on a mechanism it describes wrongly (Router fallbacks don't rescue the 429/5xx/mid-stream failures it claims cost six tenacity attempts today).
